Correction: condominium links are being rechecked

An incorrect lot-number limit in my code excluded valid candidate units. The earlier Bronx coverage gap should not be interpreted as missing public records.

By Pablo Loschi1 October 2026Corrected 21 October 2026Correction noticeSources & methods

What was wrong

The earlier version of this article presented the low Bronx condominium linkage rate as a limitation of the public records. My code searched unit lots only from 1001 to 1999. The city's documented condominium unit-lot range extends through 6999. That restriction excluded valid candidate units and explains much of the reported gap.

I am withdrawing the original interpretation while the corrected links and affected calculations are checked. The old coverage figures describe release 1.1.0 of my dataset; they do not establish that half the Bronx's condo deeds are missing from public records.

What is being checked

The review covers condominium deed matches, the mortgage searches that depend on them, and the resulting coverage and financing tables. New candidate matches need validation against complete documents. A high linkage rate alone does not establish accuracy.

The data explorer marks condominium linkage and mortgage figures as under review. Raw sales counts and recorded-price medians remain available. The existing paper PDFs and deposited datasets are preserved as dated releases, with correction notices beside the affected web summaries.

Sources and correction history

The official PLUTO dictionary, printed pages 2–3, describes condominium unit lots 1001–6999. The original article used dataset release 1.1.0. Its figures should not be used for the former borough-gap interpretation. Read the correction notice or check the dataset status.

Correction dated 21 October 2026. Original publication: 1 October 2026. The original charts are no longer offered as current reporting graphics. A revised dataset and paper results have not yet been released.
